God comforts us so that we can comfort others. How could the comfort you've received help someone else?
Paul despaired of life but learned to rely on God who raises the dead. When have you had to rely on God alone?
All God's promises find their Yes in Christ. Which promise of God do you need to hold onto?
Paul says he works with them for their joy. How can you work for someone else's joy in faith?
Paul wrote with many tears out of love. How do you speak hard truth with love?
Paul urges them to forgive and comfort the one who caused pain. Who might need your forgiveness and comfort?
We are the aroma of Christ to God. What does it mean for your life to carry the fragrance of Christ?
Paul says the believers are a letter from Christ written on hearts. What does your life "say" to others?
Our sufficiency is from God. Where do you feel inadequate, and how does this help?
We are being transformed into Christ's image from one degree of glory to another. What change has God been working in you?
"Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom." What freedom has the Spirit brought you?
God has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of his glory in Christ. How has God's light reached you?
We have this treasure in jars of clay. How does God's power show in your weakness?
Paul believed, and so he spoke. What do you believe that you could speak about?
"Our outer self is wasting away, our inner self is being renewed day by day." How does this help you not lose heart?
Paul says we walk by faith, not by sight. Where do you need to walk by faith this week?
The love of Christ controls us. How does Christ's love change what you live for?
"If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation." What is new in you because of Christ?
God has given us the ministry of reconciliation. Who could you help be reconciled to God or to others?
"Now is the day of salvation." What does that urgency mean for you?
Paul describes being sorrowful yet always rejoicing. How can both be true at once?
Paul asks them to widen their hearts. Whom might you need to open your heart to?
God says, "I will be a father to you." What does it mean to live as God's child?
Paul calls us to bring holiness to completion in the fear of God. What step toward holiness is God asking of you?
God, who comforts the downcast, comforted Paul through Titus. Who has God used to comfort you?
Godly grief produces repentance that leads to salvation without regret. What is the difference between godly grief and worldly grief?
The Macedonians gave generously out of extreme poverty. What does their example teach you?
Though Jesus was rich, he became poor for your sake. How does this shape your generosity?
Paul speaks of a fair balance where those with plenty supply those in need. Who could you help?
Paul took care to do what is honourable before the Lord and people. How do you keep integrity in money matters?
"God loves a cheerful giver." What would cheerful giving look like for you?
God is able to make all grace abound to you. How has God provided for you so you can give?
Giving overflows in many thanksgivings to God. How has someone's generosity made you thank God?
"Thanks be to God for his inexpressible gift!" What is the gift Paul means?
Paul speaks of taking every thought captive to obey Christ. What thought do you need to bring to Christ?
Paul refuses to compare himself with others. Where are you tempted to compare?
"Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord." What can you boast about in the Lord?
Paul fears they will be led astray from sincere devotion to Christ. What could pull you from simple devotion?
Paul warns that even Satan disguises himself as an angel of light. How can you tell truth from deception?
Paul lists his many hardships for the gospel. What does his endurance teach you?
Paul says he will boast of his weakness. Why?
Paul did not want anyone to think more of him than they saw. How do you resist wanting to be admired?
"My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness." Where do you need to hear this?
Paul says, "I seek not what is yours but you." What does selfless love for others look like?
Paul worried about quarrelling and pride in the church. How can you help your fellowship stay healthy?
Christ was crucified in weakness but lives by the power of God. How does this pattern apply to your life?
Paul says to examine yourselves to see whether you are in the faith. What would honest self-examination show?
"Aim for restoration, comfort one another, agree with one another, live in peace." Which do you need to work on?
Paul blesses them with the grace of Christ, the love of God and the fellowship of the Spirit. Which do you need today?
